thread:
sam: Quick sync — we're doing the RBAC tweak Wednesday 09:00 PT: remove legacy service.admin, add scoped role audit.emit and audit.view. Heads-up because this touches customer-facing audit generation + KMS key tagging. Need sign-off on schema + ingestion SLOs before roll.
maya: ack. can you paste the minimal schema you want to enforce? also we need to decide validation behavior (reject vs accept+mark). :thinking:
alex: flag: indexing everything will blow up our ES costs and query perf. we should decide searchable subset vs raw cold store. also how many tenants will opt into per-tenant KMS? that affects encryption ops.
li: draft schema below (minimal required fields). plan is to validate required keys at emit time and attach provenance metadata. nonblocking fields can be optional.
li: ```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "actor_id": "string",
  "actor_role": "string",
  "action": "string",
  "resource": {"type":"string","id":"string"},
  "outcome": "success|failure",
  "kms_key_id": "string (optional)",
  "encrypted": "boolean",
  "batch_id": "string (optional)",
  "seq": "int (optional)",
  "schema_version": "string"
}
```
li: note: include schema_version so we can forward-compat. plan: reject events missing required fields (4xx) and return event_id for customer reconciliation.
jordan: on ingestion flow: for high-volume customers we should default to batching + per-tenant sample rate. propose: 1) prefix dedupe + batching in edge, 2) token-bucket admission into hot path, 3) overflow -> cold store (compressed, cheaper) with async index job.
alex: agree. cold store could be clickhouse or parquet on object store; ES only for current 30d hot index with limited fields.
maya: customer-facing validation: we need a public schema doc and a lightweight client validator (npm/go) to reduce bad events hitting the pipeline. also define error codes: INVALID_SCHEMA (400), RATE_LIMITED (429), BACKPRESSURE_QUEUED (202).
sam: KMS questions: do we support tenant-specific KMS key per event, or just tenant-level envelope encryption? we should avoid per-event KMS calls because of TPS and cost.
li: prefer tenant-level envelope keys. store data encrypted with a dataset key per-tenant; rotate via KMS but do not call KMS for every event. only zero/rotate operations call KMS. events include kms_key_id for provenance.
security-bot: vuln triage note — if we accept unvalidated event payloads we risk injection into later evaluators. validator must strictly enforce resource.type and action enums. add a fuzz test harness.
jordan: throughput/backpressure numbers: in worst-case burst we saw 60k eps sustained 5m in test. with batch size 64 that became ~1k write ops/s. indexing + encryption ops are the bottleneck. solution: dynamic batch sizing + adaptive concurrency limiter.
ops-bot: current ingest queue depth metric: ingest.q.depth = 12k, avg ack latency = 1.8s, KMS request rate = 0.4rps (since envelope design). CPU on ingest hosts 72%.
alex: cost eyeball: if we index 100M events/month in ES with 5 fields indexed, add ~ $12k/mo cluster cost. raw cold store for 100M compressed ~ $1k/mo S3 + processing. numbers rough.
maya: policy: roll RBAC Wednesday with a feature flag so emitters must present audit.emit. enforcement trotter: warn for 2 days, then strict. will owners be notified via org-admin? need comms.
sam: plan: 1) finalize schema (li) by EOD Monday; 2) publish client validator + schema doc Tuesday; 3) rollout RBAC feature-flaged Wed; 4) monitor ingest.q.depth and error rates; auto-fallback to cold store if backpressure > threshold.
li: will add schema_version 1.0 and sample validation lib (go + npm). will also add consumer tags to events so search index can filter cheaper fields.
alex: I'll run cost sim for ES vs CH next 24h and post numbers.
jordan: I'll prototype adaptive batcher (resize based on 95p latency) and token-bucket admission.
security-bot: incident response note — add a playbook for when ingest backlog grows > 50k for >15m: 1) enable global throttle, 2) flip to cold-store-only for non-critical tenants, 3) notify SOC + assigned oncall.
sam: good. last Q: customer-facing audit validation failures — do we expose full payload in error response? we should not return sensitive fields. return event_id + minimal error string.
maya: agreed. sanitize before echoing. add audit log of validation rejects to internal channel (for ops debugging) but redact PII.
deploy-bot: canary of the emitter change passed on prod-canary-3 at 11:55. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks everyone. will follow up with a short doc and the timeline. :rocket:
